question: A man who has been successfully vasectomised is impotent, because vasectomy eliminates his ability to father children.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Impotence = inability to perform sexual intercourse (erectile dysfunction). Sterility = inability to reproduce (no viable spermatozoa in ejaculate post-vasectomy). A vasectomised man can have normal sexual intercourse — he is sterile, not impotent. These terms are not interchangeable in medicolegal reports.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Impotence refers to the inability to achieve or maintain an erection sufficient for sexual intercourse (erectile dysfunction). Sterility (or infertility) is the inability to reproduce. A vasectomised male retains full erectile and ejaculatory function — he is sterile, not impotent. Vasectomy occludes the vas deferens but has no effect on testosterone production or erectile function.
